newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Codelco Japan copper premium reflects costs -trade.
newsitem.headline: Codelco Japan copper premium reflects costs -trade.

text.p: The decision by Chilean state-owned copper giant Codelco to hold 1997 Japanese copper premiums unchanged and above its regional neighbours is understandable and reflects local delivery costs, traders said on Wednesday.

Codelco has kept next year's Japan copper premium steady at $50 a tonne over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash settlement prices, which is unchanged from this year, but above the $40 a tonne the Chileans' set for premiums to Taiwan and South Korea.
Some Tokyo traders said they were expecting lower premiums and that disgruntled Japanese users may now look to other sources of copper than Codelco.
A trader at Codelco's Seoul agent said the price gap between the two markets reflected the difference in freight costs between South Korea and Japan.

"For the third quarter of this year, Codelco's copper premium to Pusan was $12 over the CIF Rotterdam premium, while the premium to Japanese ports (Kobe/Nagoya/Yokohama) was $39 over the Rotterdam premium," he said.
"Based on this, the premium to Japan should be at least $20 a tonne more than that to South Korea," he said, adding that unloading costs and port charges were also higher in Japan.

In fact, Codelco has decided on a $40 a tonne premium for 1997 in South Korea over the base price for LME grade A copper cathodes, compared with $45 a tonne for the local market this year and Japan's $50 premium for next year.
The agent said the premium was based on CIF berth terms.
Taiwanese traders agreed that the differential with Japan's market was due to varying port, freight and other costs.
"It's normal to have a price difference between countries," a copper trader at Taiwan's Tai-I electric wire company said.
But the trader also pointed out that Codelco fixed prices are only "listed" prices and would be adjusted based on the supplier's cost considerations.
A Codelco source in Hong Kong said the copper premiums for the British colony were set at between $50-$60 a tonne CIF over the LME for next year.

Codelco copper premiums to Singapore and Malaysia will probably be in the range of $35-$40 a tonne for 1997 -- virtually unchanged from last year's level, a local metal dealer who has business with the Chilean corporation said.
Negotiations over the premiums for next year are still ongoing, but they will probably remain unchanged, another dealer agreed.
"Codelco would normally ask for a $50 premium for Singapore and Malaysia, but they are eventually forced to bring it down to around $35-$40," he said.
There was no immediate comment available from the Codelco office in Singapore.
Spot copper premiums over LME cash prices in Singapore and in Malaysia were quoted at around $110-$120 a tonne, unchanged from last Friday's levels, dealers said.
Tight stocks in the LME's Singapore warehouse, estimated by dealers at just under 2,000 tonnes, accounted for the high premiums, they said.
